Row 4: Operational Execution Audit & Analyst Q&A Highlights
WINS / DRAGS & ANALYST Q&A
What Management Did Right (Operational Wins)
  • Crossed into Non-GAAP Profitability: Generated $0.07 in Non-GAAP EPS (vs -$0.08 Street consensus), proving that clinical genomics and AI data licensing create operating leverage.
  • EBITDA Inflection: Adjusted EBITDA skyrocketed +1,633% YoY from $1.48M to $25.57M, significantly outpacing expectations.
  • MRD Quadrupling: Minimal Residual Disease volume grew +300% YoY to ~12,000 tests, capturing critical market share in cancer recurrence tracking.
  • Pharma Strategic Mega-Deals: Closed major collaborations with Merck, Moderna, and BMS, driving YTD cumulative data bookings above $550M.
What Went Wrong & Execution Headwinds
  • Revenue Trailed Whisper: Revenue of $411.54M beat consensus ($409.3M) but trailed high-end buy-side whispers ($418.0M), curbing immediate multiple expansion.
  • Negative Free Cash Flow: Operating cash flow remains negative at -$71.59M and True FCF at -$250.15M after $154.90M in SBC expense.
  • CapEx Ramp: CapEx expanded to $23.66M as lab automation and compute cluster requirements increase cash absorption.
  • Hereditary Genomics Growth Moderation: Hereditary testing revenue grew just +3% YoY, lagging high-margin oncology expansion.
Institutional Conference Call Analyst Q&A Forensic Highlights
Matt Larew (William Blair) Data & Applications Growth & Multi-Year Pharma Bookings

Question: Eric, Data & Applications grew 33% and bookings surpassed $550M YTD with the BMS deal. How much of this is upfront software licensing versus recurring milestone ARR, and what is the pipeline for additional pharma partnerships?

Executive Answer: Eric Lefkofsky (CEO) responded: 'Our data licensing model is increasingly institutionalized. Pharma partners are not buying one-off datasets; they are integrating Tempus multimodal data directly into their clinical oncology pipelines. The Merck, Moderna, and BMS collaborations are multi-year structural agreements with high renewal rates and expanding per-study licensing fees.'

Michael Ryskin (Bank of America) MRD Ramp, Reimbursement Coverage & Diagnostics Margins

Question: Jim, with MRD tests reaching 12,000 units and gross margins expanding to 64.8%, what is your timeline for broad Medicare and commercial coverage for pan-cancer recurrence monitoring?

Executive Answer: Jim Rogers (CFO) noted that Tempus has secured key MolDX local coverage determinations across colorectal and breast cancer indications, with broader pan-cancer dossiers submitted. He highlighted that lab automation is driving significant cost-of-sequencing efficiencies, allowing gross margins to scale toward 68%-70% over the next 18 months.

Dan Leonard (UBS) Cash Runway, Path to Positive FCF & CapEx Discipline

Question: With $854M in cash and marketable securities and Q3 Adjusted EBITDA hitting $25.6M, when do you anticipate crossing into positive quarterly Free Cash Flow after CapEx and lease commitments?

Executive Answer: Jim Rogers (CFO) stated that Tempus expects operating cash burn to continue contracting sequentially, targeting sustained positive operating cash flow by mid-2027. He emphasized that the $854M balance sheet provides ample runway without any need for external dilutive equity financing.
